elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly permits use by “affiliated companies of Sparkling” at Authorized Locations.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly covers “contractors and outsourced service providers acting on behalf of Sparkling or such affiliated companies.”
The operative language contains no perpetual-duration protection. It does not establish that paid-up licences are absent, so the conditional requirement cannot be treated as inapplicable.
The operative language does not state that a paid-up licence is irrevocable. The clause does not demonstrably exclude paid-up licensing.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated only for material breach.
elements.evidence: No operative language limits termination of a subscription licence to material breach, and subscription licensing is not demonstrably absent.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated only if the material breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: No cure opportunity or uncured-breach prerequisite is included, and subscription licensing is not demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Customer may transfer the licence to any successor without the licensor's consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) permits consent-free transfer only to a successor in connection with specified merger, amalgamation, reorganization, or all-or-substantially-all sale transactions, rather than to successors generally.

elements.element: Customer can extend licence coverage to affiliates on written notice without requiring the licensor's consent.
elements.evidence: The grant covers Sparkling's affiliates automatically, without requiring either notice or consent. This is broader and more favorable than coverage conditioned only on written notice.

elements.element: Customer may transfer the licence without consent to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section (d) expressly permits assignment of the Agreement, including the licence, without consent to a successor in connection with a merger, amalgamation, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business.

result.reason: The redline achieves the fallback through automatic affiliate coverage and a consent-free M&A successor exception, but omits all required paid-up and subscription protections and does not provide the preferred unrestricted successor-transfer right. It is not minimal because it also grants Garman a reciprocal consent-free M&A assignment right, an unrelated commercial benefit not required by either Customer position. That change also prevents preservation of unrelated intent. Retaining the unqualified phrase “non-transferable” in the grant while later allowing transfer of the licence creates avoidable drafting tension, although the express assignment exception is likely operative. The margin comment cannot cure the omitted operative protections.
